heroText: Asuncion is Paraguay's warm, understated capital on the Paraguay River, with colonial fragments, leafy neighborhoods and a slower pace than many regional capitals. Start at Palacio de los Lopez, walk the Costanera de Asuncion, then visit Casa de la Independencia for national history. Silvio Pettirossi airport sits northeast of town, making Villa Morra or Carmelitas practical hotel bases.

areas.name: Centro Historico
areas.text: Centro Historico is best for civic sights, plazas and daytime walks, though many visitors prefer newer districts for evenings.

areas.name: Villa Morra
areas.text: Villa Morra is the easiest first base, with hotels, restaurants, shopping and safer evening movement than the old centre.

areas.name: Carmelitas
areas.text: Carmelitas is strong for nightlife, malls and modern restaurants, useful for social stays and business trips.

areas.name: Recoleta
areas.text: Recoleta is a quieter residential district with embassies, restaurants and good access between the centre and newer areas.

areas.name: Las Mercedes
areas.text: Las Mercedes is close to the old centre but calmer, with guesthouses, cafes and short taxi rides to key sights.

airports.text: Silvio Pettirossi airport is northeast of Asuncion near Luque; transfers are usually simple but traffic can slow peak routes.

airportTransfer.value: 20-40 min by taxi or ride-hail to Villa Morra or central Asuncion
airportTransfer.distance: about 12 km northeast of central Asuncion

stayOverview: Villa Morra is the safest first Asuncion base for restaurants and hotels, while Carmelitas suits nightlife and business. Centro Historico is best by day, Recoleta is calmer, and Las Mercedes offers guesthouse stays near the old centre.
hotelIntro: Asuncion hotel choice depends on evenings: Villa Morra and Carmelitas are modern and practical, Centro Historico is useful for daytime sights, Recoleta is quieter, and Las Mercedes gives a smaller-scale base near central routes.
rentalCars: A rental car helps for lake towns and countryside stops, but taxis and rideshare are easier inside Asuncion.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Villa Morra for a first stay if restaurants, shopping, hotel choice and easier evening movement are priorities.

travelTips.title: Heat
travelTips.text: Asuncion can be very hot and humid, so plan outdoor walks early and use taxis in the afternoon.

travelTips.title: Cash
travelTips.text: Carry some guarani for small purchases, markets and taxis, even when cards work at hotels and larger restaurants.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Aregua and Lake Ypacarai are the easiest short escapes when you want crafts, lake views and a slower pace.

history.text: More than 400 schools, metallurgic factories and the first railroad service in South America were built during the López presidency.
The fort that preceded it was established with the same name on 15 August 1537, by Juan de Salazar de Espinosa, the day on which the Catholic Church commemorates the Assumption of Mary.
In 1542 natives destroyed Buenos Aires, and the Spaniards there fled to Asunción.
The licentious life of the colonists led a priest to describe it in 1545 as the "paradise of Muhammad", a phrase that became one of the city's enduring historical epithets.
In 1731 an uprising under José de Antequera y Castro was one of the first rebellions against Spanish colonial rule.
The event influenced the independence of Paraguay, which subsequently materialized in 1811.
Under the rule of Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia (in office 1813–1840) roads were built throughout the city and the streets were named.
After López died in 1862, his son Francisco Solano López became the new president and led the country through the disastrous Paraguayan War that lasted for five years (1864–1870).
On 1 January 1869, the capital city Asunción fell to Brazilian forces led by Gen.
A tramway in Asunción opened in 1871, initially using horse-drawn trams and steam-powered trams, with electric trams being introduced in 1913.

In August 2004, Asunción suffered the greatest tragedy in the history of the country, after the Chaco War, with the infamous blaze at Ycua Bolaños, a supermarket fire that claimed more than 400 lives.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Thus the city became the center of a large Spanish colonial province comprising part of Brazil, present-day Paraguay and northeastern Argentina.
